text:
catie: quick RFC follow-up — during a mid-canary we saw micro-quality wobble after switching to fp8 profiles for a high-context customer. not catastrophic but user-visible turn-to-turn jitter. any ideas on safer rollout patterns?
josh: yup, saw a similar pattern in bench runs. seems like per-layer activation scale shifts + kv-cache encoding differences cause earlier tokens to nudge topk.
anita: customer telemetry: top1-churn + 12% on the first response after switch, bigram-fidelity dropped too. i dumped a few traces (link: https://go/shadow-traces/abc123) — consistent pattern.
leo: my 2c: split rollout into distinct phases: dry-shadow -> calibration-warmup -> session-boundary-upgrade. avoid atomic mid-session upgrades.
catie: flesh that out?
leo: sure:
  1) dry-shadow: run target precision path in shadow mode (no responses served), collect degscore & activation stats over N traces.
  2) calibrate: compute per-layer affine correction (scale/bias) from shadow vs baseline on short window (32-128 tokens). apply correction to activations on switch.
  3) micro-warmup: for first M sessions after switch, route a small fraction of traffic through target precision but return baseline responses; use live traces to verify degscore within tolerance.
  4) session-boundary only: schedule upgrades only at session end; allow downgrades mid-session only if degscore spikes.
anita: calibration at activation level sounds good. important to ensure kv-cache entries are stored with precision tag so we can detect mixed-precision resumes.
josh: also consider ephemeral micro-batches to pre-populate KV in target precision before serving the first post-upgrade request — avoids cold kv mismatch.
leo: agreed. micro-batch warmup pseudocode:```python
# before flipping route
for trace in warmup_traces:
    run_forward(trace, precision=target, populate_kv=True, discard_outputs=True)
# then flip at session boundary
```
catie: operational knobs we should expose per-route: allow_shadow_percent, calib_window_tokens, warmup_traces_count, session_upgrade_only=true, rollback_consecutive_failures, degscore_threshold. default conservative.
nenote: example route config:```yaml
precision_policy:
  default: fp16
  allowed_targets: [fp8, int8, 4bit]
  rollout_plan:
    shadow_percent: 10
    calib_window_tokens: 64
    warmup_traces: 8
    session_upgrade_only: true
    rollback_after_consecutive_failures: 3
    degscore_threshold: 0.05 # relative
```
anita: telemetry we need: per-session pre/post perplexity delta, topk-churn, ngram-fidelity, kv-population-hits, and a synthetic similarity score for long-context drift. also mark whether session used mixed-precision KV.
josh: for automation: we can precompute an expected delta offline by re-running sample corpora through both precisions and produce a per-route risk score. use that during canary decisions.
leo: runtime API idea: /v1/routes/{id}/precision_rollout [PUT] with body containing policy above plus dry_run flag. policy engine should enforce session-boundary=true for upgrades unless override with explicit consent.
ops-bot: reminder: any change touching KV format or persistent cache layout requires eng-runtime migration plan and CI gating. See https://go/redwood-eng-runtime-cq for checklist.
catie: edge-case: long-lived sessions (e.g., document editing). recommend disallow upgrades for sessions > X tokens, or require explicit session-level approval.
anita: agree. we should also provide a graceful decay when we detect increasing drift: exponential backoff from target precision and auto-rollback after K bad sessions.
josh: also add a lightweight per-layer variance monitor in runtime that flags layers with significant activation distribution shifts; can trigger adaptive per-layer fallbacks (e.g., keep layer L at baseline precision).
leo: that gets more complex but would be powerful: per-layer pinning in rollout_plan: pinned_layers: [3,5,7].
catie: operational action items: 1) add telemetry hooks for pre/post session degscore 2) implement dry-shadow harness in runtime 3) prototype activation-affine calibration kernel (eng-runtime) 4) update route API and console UX.
anita: i'll own telemetry + canary trace collection.
josh: i'll sketch the dry-shadow infra and risk scorer.
leo: i'll prototype the micro-warmup flow and per-layer pin mechanism.
catie: OK please +1 in channel when prototypes ready; aim for quick canary next week. :rocket:
josh: +1
anita: +1
leo: +1
ops-bot: note: flagging this thread for follow-up in eng-ml weekly sync.
catie: thanks everyone — will summarize for RFC follow-up.
